component.name: RAVE
component.summary: Open music player with replaceable sources

description.p: RAVE is an open-source desktop music player built on Nuclear. It keeps Nuclear's plugin and theme ecosystem while developing an independent interface and source-aware listening experience.

ul.li: Search for music across multiple sources
Choose and inspect playback sources
Extend the player with Nuclear-compatible plugins
Customize the interface with built-in and community themes
Release metadata now consistently identifies version 1.50.0, production-only warnings are removed, and the RAVE documentation records installation, distinguishing features, and known limitations.
The mini-player progress bar is now a three-pixel bottom edge with a hover-only thumb, while its content is vertically centered with balanced spacing.
The mini-player window now ends directly below its horizontal control bar, removing the unused strip beneath the progress line.
The mini player has been redesigned as a narrow Spotify-style horizontal control bar with drag handle, compact artwork, inline playback controls, volume, and bottom-edge progress.
The mini player now fills the RAVE window without a transparent outer frame, follows the active application theme, and adds an inline volume control beside Next.
The mini player now uses a frameless Liquid Glass layout with artwork-tinted translucency, a refractive rim, hover-only window controls, a glowing seek bar, and focused playback controls.
The mini player is now genuinely compact, uses space more efficiently, and has complete Russian translations for its queue, controls, lyrics, and audio output.
Added complete Russian translations for Library Loudness and LAN Sync, including navigation, forms, statuses, and notifications.
Corrected the Russian dashboard heading for editorial playlists.
Artist discographies now sort chronologically by complete release dates and use locale-aware natural title ordering, with undated releases kept at the end.

Artist discographies now fetch missing track counts and durations before classifying ambiguous releases, so one-to-three-track releases no longer remain under Albums merely because a provider labelled them as albums.
Removed the pervasive offset shadows from cards, buttons, dialogs, menus, artwork, and session screens while preserving borders and focus states for a cleaner RAVE interface.
RAVE now uses Manrope for its interface and Unbounded for display headings, with complete Latin and Cyrillic subsets bundled locally for a more distinctive identity without external font requests.

Reduced the initial JavaScript payload by loading HLS playback and settings views only when needed, tree-shaking unused UI components, and keeping test utilities out of production bundles. Tailwind now scans only the source packages required by each application build.
Reduced unnecessary React renders, duplicate query refreshes, and disabled-integration wakeups through narrow Zustand subscriptions, shared query defaults, and an on-demand Discord heartbeat.
Removed unused Nuclear-only release automation and redundant runtime dependencies while keeping compatibility-critical plugin and theme identifiers intact.
Internal TanStack and Zustand developer tools are now excluded from production builds while remaining available through the development shortcut.
RAVE now loads background integrations after the first render and reuses one cached history request across personalized widgets.
Prompted Playlist turns Russian or English requests into visible local rules for mood, offline availability, years, duration, and excluded artists before creating an editable playlist.
Release Radar scans favorite artists through installed metadata providers and shows recent and upcoming releases with a six-hour query cache to protect startup and provider performance.
Favorite tracks now have smart library filters for offline availability, mood, personal tags, and tracks that still need organization.
The RAVE dashboard can now resurface forgotten favorites that have not been played for 30 days, including older saved tracks that have never been played.
RAVE Weekly adds a private rolling seven-day listening summary with minutes, unique tracks, artists, discoveries, and the week's top artist, calculated entirely from local history.
Individual tracks can now be excluded from the local taste profile, allowing background, guest, sleep, or children's listening without distorting recommendations.
RAVE can now pause recommendations for a track for 7, 30, or 90 days without permanently blocking it, with an immediate restore action in the track menu.
Smart Source can now keep a configurable reserve of two or three resolved candidates per track for faster recovery when the active stream fails, while respecting data saver mode.
The queue now explains when the next track was selected by auto-radio or taste-aware smart shuffle, making automatic choices visible instead of opaque.
RAVE can pre-analyze favorite tracks, cache clipping-safe ReplayGain values, and apply the saved adjustment on later playback without repeatedly analyzing audio in real time.
RAVE adds a data saver mode that caps preferred stream bitrate, suppresses artwork from metadata responses, disables backup-source preloading, and avoids eager audio buffering.
RAVE devices can now import playlists, listening history, and non-sensitive preferences directly over the local network using an explicit preview-and-confirm flow and optional session pairing.
RAVE adds an always-on-top mini player that keeps playback uninterrupted while showing artwork, controls, source quality, volume, seek position, and the next queue entries.
RAVE adds built-in Libre.fm scrobbling with signed Scrobbling 2.0 requests, standard qualification thresholds, now-playing updates, and a persistent retry outbox.
Smart Source can now learn rejected live, remix, and slowed versions across tracks and automatically exclude them whenever a suitable alternative is available.
RAVE adds a configurable Dislike shortcut that blocks the current track from recommendations and immediately continues playback with the next queue item.
RAVE lets listeners pin favorite playlists so they remain at the top while preserving the selected sort order for everything else.
RAVE can import YouTube and YouTube Music playlists directly from their URLs using its built-in yt-dlp integration, without requiring a separate playlist plugin.
RAVE starts faster by reusing compiled plugins from a versioned content-addressed cache and keeps diagnostic logs focused by suppressing transport internals and routine successful HTTP traffic.
RAVE is now formally documented and packaged as an independent Nuclear fork, with preserved upstream attribution, separate contribution rules, and RAVE-only release targets.
RAVE now classifies singles, EPs, albums, and compilations consistently from track count, per-track duration, total duration, artist credits, and release-year metadata.
RAVE adds a filterable and sortable artist discography, groups duplicate releases while preserving variants, learns from wrong-version feedback, and supports selecting an audio output device.
RAVE reduces startup work and unnecessary interface updates by loading screens, language packs, and developer tools on demand, narrowing state subscriptions, and reusing the backend HTTP client.
Artist pages now separate full albums from singles and EPs while remaining compatible with metadata providers that do not expose release types yet.

RAVE adds desktop-style double-click playback, bulk playlist actions, shuffle and Smart Shuffle, complete artist credits, quick source switching, resumable downloads, system media controls, and a personalized For You section.
RAVE adds a configurable start page, favorite sorting, bulk track selection, and playlist search across descriptions, tags, tracks, artists, albums, and notes.
RAVE Source Inspector explains Smart Source scoring, shows stream quality, switches between candidates, and copies a privacy-safe playback diagnostic report.
RAVE opens faster by hydrating independent data in parallel and moving optional work beyond the first render, while preventing duplicate dashboard cards and overlapping stream recovery attempts.
RAVE reduces playback-time disk writes, avoids unrelated interface rerenders, and caches taste-ranking calculations without changing playback behavior.
RAVE Personal Listening adds playback resume, Listen Later, recommendation filters, optional queue cleanup, sleep timers, moods, private tags and notes, family filtering, and a local taste profile.
RAVE now keeps one latest entry per track in listening history and lets listeners exclude artists from Radio and Mix recommendations.
RAVE is now the only bundled basic theme; legacy Nuclear theme selections migrate safely to RAVE while custom and marketplace themes remain supported.
RAVE Intelligence adds undoable queue editing, Replay playlists, filtered Mix modes, prepared backup streams, and real crossfade transitions while preserving Nuclear defaults.
RAVE Sessions adds pairing-protected local listening rooms with guest permissions, queue voting, QR invitations, participants, and an activity history.
RAVE now ranks streaming sources by title and duration match, bitrate, response time, reliability, and user preferences.
RAVE now identifies itself as a Nuclear fork, enforces a desktop content security policy, and reports failures when every streaming source is unavailable.
The RAVE Windows launcher now resolves its project folder relative to itself and discovers Git in common installation locations.
RAVE identity is now consistent in Linux launchers, AppStream metadata, MCP responses, and exported logs.
RAVE now keeps remote stream verification opt-in and no longer registers the Nuclear updater at runtime.
RAVE now safely restores local favorites even when one saved collection is malformed or unreadable.
RAVE can now start a continuous radio queue from any track through its context menu.
RAVE playlist URL import now falls back to another compatible provider when the preferred service is unavailable.
RAVE queue now separates listening history, the current track, and upcoming tracks while preserving drag-and-drop controls.
RAVE now falls back across installed streaming providers when the active source cannot find or play a track.
RAVE search now merges available metadata providers, ranks exact matches first, removes duplicates, and keeps working when one source fails.

description.p: Introduces the independent RAVE identity and default visual theme.
